findings.failure_path: A tool is used, then its authorization is revoked while the loop continues. The rule says to prefer marking it unavailable and “never” remove a tool cited by current history, while the gateway requires revoked or newly unauthorized material to be removed through mandatory invalidation. An implementation following the dispatch rule can retain the revoked schema or related prompt material and continue the loop, violating the stated privacy/authorization invariant.
findings.smallest_fix: Qualify history-preserving eviction with the gateway’s mandatory-invalidation override: on authorization, privacy, safety, or policy invalidation, remove the revoked material, reset the cache baseline/generation, and restart or fail closed if retained history cannot remain valid without that tool.

challenge_focus: Fresh full adversarial pass on the post-fix lane-3 candidate, not a confirm-my-fixes pass: (1) normalized cache-usage counters — a provider shape (inclusive total, nested subsets, absent fields) that still double-counts, under-counts, or misclassifies a route; (2) the batch capability decision — a provider path where an ambiguous submission still duplicates billing or orphans accepted work; (3) the tool-set boundary and mandatory-invalidation clause — surviving text licensing in-flight mutation, suffix-only reuse, or retained revoked material; (4) plan-then-execute binding and the trifecta negative test — an injected change that still reaches an external action; (5) the delegation fan-out gate, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission or over-broad cost; (6) register anchors, receipts, rows — stale locators, unsupported claims, contradictions; (7) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
